description: Database-backed worker backend for Django's Tasks framework (django.tasks, Django 6.0+). Background tasks run on the database you already have. No broker to provision, secure or back up.
rules: Requires Django 6.0 or later and Python 3.12 or later.
Add django_ox to INSTALLED_APPS and set BACKEND to django_ox.backend.OxBackend in the TASKS setting.
Run python manage.py migrate django_ox before starting a worker.
Start a worker with the ox_worker management command. It is a separate process from the web server, and tasks only execute while a worker is running.
Tasks are ordinary django.tasks tasks. django-ox adds nothing to learn on the producer side, so task functions stay portable across django.tasks backends.

enqueue() is a single INSERT on the default database connection. A task enqueued inside transaction.atomic() becomes visible to workers only when that transaction commits, and disappears on rollback, so transaction.on_commit() is not needed.
Workers claim tasks with SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED on PostgreSQL and MySQL 8 or later, and with an atomic compare-and-set on databases without SKIP LOCKED, including SQLite.
Execution is at-least-once, so tasks should be written to be idempotent.
Use ox_health to check worker and queue health, and ox_prune to delete finished task rows older than a cutoff.
Install with pip install django-ox. Configuration lives in the TASKS setting; the smallest working entry is TASKS = {"default": {"BACKEND": "django_ox.backend.OxBackend"}}.
Backend OPTIONS are MAX_ATTEMPTS (default 3), LOCK_TIMEOUT (300 seconds), BACKOFF_INITIAL (5 seconds), BACKOFF_MAX (600 seconds) and SCHEDULES. QUEUES sits beside OPTIONS, not inside it.

An attempt is consumed when a worker claims the task, so a worker dying mid-run counts as an attempt. The retry delay after attempt n is BACKOFF_INITIAL * 2 ** (n - 1), capped at BACKOFF_MAX, with no jitter.

LOCK_TIMEOUT bounds how long a worker may stop refreshing its lease, not how long a task may run. A worker renews the lease every LOCK_TIMEOUT / 3 seconds, so a long task on a live worker is not reclaimed.

Recurring tasks are declared in OPTIONS["SCHEDULES"] with a dotted task path and a five-field cron expression. Every running worker dispatches schedules and a unique constraint makes each tick fire once, so there is no separate scheduler process.
The task function is called outside any transaction. A task that needs select_for_update() or atomic writes opens its own transaction.atomic().
ox_worker --concurrency N is a thread pool inside one process. For CPU-bound tasks run several worker processes with --concurrency 1.
There is no revocation or cancellation API after enqueue, and tasks are stored on the default database.
For tests, point TASKS at django.tasks.backends.immediate.ImmediateBackend or django.tasks.backends.dummy.DummyBackend instead of django-ox.
Batches and unique tasks are not in django-ox. They are in Oxpull Pro, a separate paid package. django_ox.stats and ox_health are in the free package.
